Red-proofing a lint check by planting a literal in a real tree file and restoring with `git checkout --` also silently reverted a legitimate earlier edit in the same file (select.md, this run): the restore goes back to HEAD, not to the pre-plant working state. Fix idea: red-proof against a scratch copy under mktemp -d (lint accepts file content via the checked tree only, so instead plant in a file with NO other pending edits), or restore with `git stash`-free surgical removal of just the planted line.
